extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to publishers/editors (academic and literary writers)
extracted.subtask_description: General guidance on what a manuscript is and practical/formatting considerations authors should follow when preparing work for submission to publishers, editors, or repositories (covers literary and academic contexts, plus preprint considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Many publishers still require authors to submit manuscripts formatted according to their respective guidelines. Writers who intend to submit a manuscript should determine what the relevant writing standards are, and follow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting varies greatly depending on the type of work and the particular publisher, editor or producer; always check and follow the publisher's specific guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers' standards take precedence over style guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Although style guides are key references, individual publishers' standards always take precedence over style guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a recognized style guide as a reference because 'virtually all professional editors work closely with one of them', but defer to any explicit publisher/editor requirements when they conflict with the style guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of style guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Style guides are key references since virtually all professional editors work closely with one of them in editing a manuscript for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult an appropriate style guide for consistent grammar, punctuation, citation, and editorial conventions, especially where publisher instructions are silent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard manuscript format for literary submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers of literary works such as short stories and poetry often expect submissions in standard manuscript format, which is easily distinguishable from most published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting literary pieces, follow conventional 'standard manuscript' conventions (check publisher specifics) rather than the typographic layout of final published works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital preparation and typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Today manuscripts are usually prepared using computers with digital typesetting or word processing software (historically they were handwritten or typewritten).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare manuscripts using modern digital tools and appropriate file formats unless a publisher requests otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for final print (layout, proofreading, prepress proofing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A future 'final print' must be planned — with better layout, proofreading, prepress proofing, etc. — that will replace the 'preprinted manuscript'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should anticipate and prepare for additional professional layout and proofing steps that occur after acceptance and prior to final publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint distribution and publisher's preprint status
rubrics_metrics.description: An ordinary manuscript only becomes a 'publisher's preprint' if it somehow gets distributed beyond the authors. In a peer review context: if an author prepares a manuscript on their computer and submits it to a publisher for review but it is not accepted, there cannot be a 'publisher's preprint'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a manuscript is considered a preprint depends on distribution and publisher policies; check publisher policy on preprints and distribution before sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating authorship via repository or legal deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: To demonstrate authorship, an author can upload a version of their work to a repository before full publication. An alternative could be to use a legal deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional repositories, subject repositories, or legal deposit mechanisms if you need public evidence of authorship prior to formal publication; verify repository and publisher policies.
